NYS Schools: Summary Tables and Plots

library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Find the data when this file is in the project root or script folder.
data_path <- "data/processed/merged_data.csv"
if (!file.exists(data_path)) {
  data_path <- "../data/processed/merged_data.csv"
}
merged_data <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2016 is the latest year with both school and county poverty data.
analysis_data <- merged_data |>
  filter(year == 2016) |>
  mutate(
    lunch_rate = per_free_lunch + per_reduced_lunch,
    poverty_group = factor(poverty_group,
                           levels = c("low", "medium", "high"))
  )

Task 5: Summary tables

We use 2016 to compare schools and counties in the same year. County poverty data are missing for 2017. Missing observations are excluded from each calculation. Lunch eligibility is weighted by enrollment; test scores are averages of school mean scores.

county_summary <- analysis_data |>
  filter(!is.na(county_name)) |>
  group_by(county_name) |>
  summarise(
    total_enrollment = sum(total_enroll, na.rm = TRUE),
    lunch_percent = weighted.mean(lunch_rate, total_enroll,
                                  na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    poverty_percent = first(county_per_poverty) * 100,
    mean_ela = mean(mean_ela_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_math = mean(mean_math_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

county_summary |>
  select(county_name, total_enrollment, lunch_percent, poverty_percent) |>
  arrange(county_name) |>
  kable(digits = 1,
        col.names = c("County", "Enrollment", "Free/reduced lunch (%)",
                      "Poverty (%)"),
        caption = "County enrollment, lunch eligibility, and poverty, 2016")

Five highest- and five lowest-poverty counties

top_five <- county_summary |>
  filter(!is.na(poverty_percent)) |>
  arrange(desc(poverty_percent), county_name) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  mutate(group = "Highest poverty")

bottom_five <- county_summary |>
  filter(!is.na(poverty_percent)) |>
  arrange(poverty_percent, county_name) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  mutate(group = "Lowest poverty")

bind_rows(top_five, bottom_five) |>
  select(group, county_name, poverty_percent, lunch_percent,
         mean_ela, mean_math) |>
  kable(digits = 1,
        col.names = c("Group", "County", "Poverty (%)",
                      "Free/reduced lunch (%)", "Mean ELA", "Mean math"),
        caption = "Counties at the two ends of the poverty distribution, 2016")

Task 6: Simple visualizations

Lunch eligibility and school test performance

Each point represents a school. The lines show associations, not causal effects. A z-score of zero is the statewide school average for that year.

analysis_data |>
  pivot_longer(c(math_z, ela_z),
               names_to = "subject", values_to = "z_score") |>
  mutate(subject = recode(subject, math_z = "Math", ela_z = "ELA")) |>
  filter(!is.na(lunch_rate), !is.na(z_score)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = lunch_rate, y = z_score)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "darkred") +
  facet_wrap(~ subject) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(title = "Higher lunch eligibility is associated with lower test scores",
       subtitle = "Schools in 2016",
       x = "Students eligible for free or reduced-price lunch",
       y = "Test score (z-score)") +
  theme_minimal()

County performance by poverty group

We first average schools within each county, then average counties within each poverty group. Each county receives equal weight. Poverty groups are the existing categories in the transformed dataset.

county_scores <- analysis_data |>
  filter(!is.na(county_name), !is.na(poverty_group)) |>
  group_by(county_name, poverty_group) |>
  summarise(
    math_z = mean(math_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    ela_z = mean(ela_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

group_scores <- county_scores |>
  group_by(poverty_group) |>
  summarise(
    math_z = mean(math_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    ela_z = mean(ela_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

group_scores |>
  pivot_longer(c(math_z, ela_z),
               names_to = "subject", values_to = "mean_z") |>
  mutate(subject = recode(subject, math_z = "Math", ela_z = "ELA")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = poverty_group, y = mean_z)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray40") +
  facet_wrap(~ subject) +
  labs(title = "Test performance differs across county poverty groups",
       subtitle = "County averages in 2016",
       x = "County poverty group",
       y = "Average test score (z-score)") +
  theme_minimal()
